title: Runtime tool conductor: context boundary enforcement and halt policy for recursive tool chains
creator: Maya Chen
description: Design and implement a Runtime Tool Conductor that enforces context and recursion boundaries for multi-tool chains. The conductor is responsible for: (1) tracking token/context consumption per request across chained tool calls; (2) identifying likely recursion or runaway loops via heuristics and lightweight provenance checks; (3) applying circuit-breaker halt/backoff policies (soft-fail vs hard abort) with graceful streaming termination; (4) merging partial results from streaming tool outputs into a consistent structured output contract; and (5) providing a compatibility shim so older tooling interfaces (synchronous result, no provenance) can participate safely. This ticket covers design, implementation, tests, and rollout plan. Goal: reduce incidents where chained tools cause unbounded recursion or excess cost while preserving low-latency streaming for normal flows.
acceptance_criteria: Conductor enforces a configurable per-request context budget and rejects additional tool invocations that would exceed the budget with a clear structured error
Heuristic recursion detector flags >95% of synthetic recursion loops in unit/integration tests and triggers soft-fail policy by default
Streaming tool outputs can be merged incrementally and emitted to the client with stable ordering guarantees under the structured-output contract
Compatibility shim allows legacy sync-only tools to be attached without changing their code; integration test coverage for shimed tools >90%
Rollback path documented and automatic feature flag for gradual rollout; no P0 regressions in staging after 48 hours of soak
implementation_notes: Conductor will be an execution-layer component sitting between the request router and the tool invocation subsystem
Maintain an append-only provenance log for the request with lightweight fingerprints (tool id, input-hash, parent-call-id) to detect repeated call patterns
Recursion heuristic: combination of repeated fingerprints (same tool+similarly hashed input) and call-graph depth; use exponential backoff counters before hard abort
Context budget: tokens + time + KV-cache footprint; default token budget = 4096 but configurable per customer/route
Streaming merge: incremental JSON lines with sequence metadata and finalization marker; support partial rollups into structured output schemas (results[], metadata)
Compatibility shim: adapter that wraps sync tools exposing a streaming façade, buffering up to N chunks or until flush conditions
Expose metrics: conductor.halts.count, conductor.soft_fail.count, conductor.recurse_detected.rate, conductor.buffered_bytes.gauge
Expose a debug trace endpoint to reconstruct the conductor provenance for a single request (feature-flagged in staging)
Will require minor additions to the SDKs: structured error types and streaming finalization hook
progress_updates: 2026-02-20: Drafted initial spec and shared with runtime team; scoped work into two phases (detect vs. mitigation)
2026-02-24: Spike complete for lightweight provenance fingerprints; memory overhead measured ~120 bytes/request in worst-case; acceptable
2026-02-28: Implemented initial recursion heuristic prototype in local runtime branch; detects synthetic loops reliably in unit harness
2026-03-03: Built streaming merge prototype that emits incremental JSON-Lines + finalization marker; validated ordering against a mocked client stream
2026-03-06: Compatibility shim prototype implemented for legacy sync tools; added adapter tests and verified no behavior changes for existing tools
2026-03-09: Added metrics endpoints and integrated with existing console dashboards; started drafting rollout plan and feature flags

Liam O'Connor (Eng) 2026-03-04: Prototype shows edge-case where buffered legacy shim can increase latency under backpressure; plan to add backpressure-aware flush

testing_plan: Unit tests for provenance fingerprint generation and fingerprint collision bounds
Property-based tests for recursion detector covering randomized call graphs
Integration tests simulating mix of streaming and sync tools with varying latency and chunk sizes
Load tests validating memory overhead and metrics under 1k RPS with typical tool fanout patterns
Chaos/chaotic-tool tests that intentionally misbehave (infinite loop, repeated calls) to validate halting and rollback behavior
Staging soak for 72 hours behind feature flag with Canary rollout to 10% of production traffic
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (staging): enable for internal customers and non-critical routes; collect metrics and traces
Phase 2 (canary): enable for 10% of production routes with conservative budgets; monitor console and alert on increases in soft_fail.count
Phase 3 (gradual): expand to customers who opted into improved safety; provide SDK update notes for structured errors
Rollback: disable feature flag; conductor includes quick-mode toggle to convert hard-aborts to soft-fails during rollback
